Page Designer: https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/paas/app-builder-cloud/visual-builder-developer/use-page-designer.html
The architectural move that should happen before more features pile on
Right now everything lives as loose Functions in one or two Web Library FieldFormula records — JSONEscape, GetRequireConfigJs, GetDesignerBodyHtml, GetDesignerCss, GetDesignerViewModelJs, GenerateSaveUrl, GetLayoutPercentages, RenderPageDesign, plus the iScripts themselves. That's held together fine at this size, but "image tools, styling, all the JET things" is exactly the kind of growth that turns a flat function list into an unmanageable wall of string-concatenation code. This is the natural point to move into Application Packages — real classes, proper encapsulation, one concern per class instead of one giant record.
A structure that would scale with everything you listed:
OU_PAGEBUILDER (App Package) │ ├── Utils │ │ │ └── JsonUtil - escape/parse helpers, wraps JsonObject/JsonArray quirks │ ├── Model │ │ │ ├── PageDesign - one design: header + rows + cols, loads/saves itself │ │ │ ├── PageRow - row: layout code, bgColor, bgImage, cols[] │ │ │ └── PageCol - col: contentType, textValue, imageUrl, linkUrl, linkLabel │ ├── Layout │ │ │ └── LayoutEngine - GetPercentages(), the single source of truth both designer JS and server render pull from (see below) │ ├── Render │ │ │ ├── PageRenderer - RenderPageDesign(), pure HTML output for the view iScript │ │ │ └── DesignerAssets - GetCss(), GetViewModelJs(), GetBodyHtml() │ ├── Security │ │ │ └── AccessCheck - CheckDesignerAccess(), CheckViewAccess() - one place, not copy-pasted across every iScript │ └── Storage │ └── DesignRepository - all the SQLExec/CreateRowset CRUD, so swapping delete-and-reinsert for a real diff-based update later touches one class, not every iScript
The genuinely high-value part of this isn't tidiness for its own sake — it's that LayoutEngine.GetPercentages() becomes the one place the ten layout codes are defined, instead of today's situation where the same list is hand-duplicated in GetDesignerViewModelJs()'s JavaScript array and GetLayoutPercentages()'s PeopleCode Evaluate. Add an eleventh layout today and you edit two places by hand with two different syntaxes — that's exactly the kind of drift that causes the designer preview to silently disagree with the live page. One authoritative source, exposed to both sides (PeopleCode calls it directly; the JS gets it serialized as JSON at page-render time, same pattern as PGDSN_DATA), removes that whole failure mode.
The actual roadmap, grouped
Foundational (do before or alongside the refactor)
Permission checks — still commented out everywhere Delete-row / reorder — built but unverified IMAGE/LINK content types — built but unverified
Content & authoring
Real inline editing (replacing the prompt() placeholders) — text areas, an image picker, a link form Image upload via PeopleTools Attachments vs. plain URL — this decision was flagged early and deferred; worth revisiting now that the data model is proven Rich text (a lightweight WYSIWYG for the HTML content type, or accept plain Markdown-ish text and convert server-side) HTML sanitization for the HTML content type, once real content editors other than you are trusted with it
Styling
Per-row/per-col padding, alignment, text color — currently hardcoded in the view CSS Reusable style presets rather than free-form color pickers (keeps output visually consistent) Responsive behavior — right now columns don't stack on narrow screens; oj-flex needs breakpoint classes or you hand-roll a media query
"All the JET things"
Actual JET components beyond oj-button in rendered output (cards, avatars, carousels) — each one is a fresh round of the RequireJS path-hunting we did for ojtable/Preact, so budget real time per component Deciding, per component, whether it's worth JET's overhead at all versus plain HTML+CSS (this thread's biggest lesson: JET earns its keep for genuinely interactive widgets, not for things plain HTML already does — like the view page you just simplified away from JET entirely)
Platform maturity
Reorder via drag-and-drop (currently sequence numbers only move via delete/re-add) Publish/draft workflow (PGDSN_STATUS exists but isn't enforced anywhere yet — should Inactive designs 404 on the view iScript?) Cloning a design as a starting template for a new one
oj-checkboxset — not a fit for the current registry, and I'd skip it rather than force it
Oracle's docs are explicit: oj-checkboxset needs either multiple child <oj-option> elements (one per checkbox) or a DataProvider — there's no flat-attribute way to configure its choices. That's structurally the same problem oj-select-single hit earlier this session (the one that led nowhere and got dropped), just wearing a different component name. Our PageRenderer/registry model only knows how to write flat attributes onto a single tag (plus the one special-cased slot for oj-button's label) — it has no concept of "render N child elements from a list," so oj-checkboxset would 404 into the exact same dead end, just with a different failure signature.
Worth being honest that supporting it for real is a genuinely separate feature — a new "options list" prop type where ComponentProps holds an array of {value, label} pairs and PageRenderer loops over them generating <oj-option> children (or, more robustly given the DataProvider preference in the docs, wiring up a small inline script per instance the way the JET-component-as-widget approach originally sketched). That's real, scoped work, not a five-line registry addition — worth doing deliberately later if you actually need multi-choice inputs, rather than bolting it onto this pattern and rediscovering the same wall.
